blocks.text: KING OVER ISRAEL AFTER SAUL · UNITED KINGDOM
Ish-bosheth. Two years over Israel, with Abner beside him.
House of Saul 2nd of 4 in The united kingdom
“Abner, captain of Saul's host, took Ish-bosheth to Mahanaim and made him king over Gilead, the Ashurites…”
THE UNITED KINGDOM: 4 RULERS SAUL → SOLOMON
After Saul died on Gilboa, Abner brought Ish-bosheth over the Jordan to Mahanaim and made him king. He was forty years old. 2 Samuel 2:8–10
From the textScripture records no anointing for him and names no prophet in his reign. 2 Samuel 2:8–10
ON THE WORLD STAGE: Judah under David · The Philistines

Abner, captain of Saul's host, took Ish-bosheth to Mahanaim and made him king over Gilead, the Ashurites, Jezreel, Ephraim and Benjamin, “and over all Israel”. “But the house of Judah followed David.” 2 Samuel 2:8–10

When Ish-bosheth challenged Abner over Rizpah, Saul's concubine, Abner swore to give the kingdom to David, and Ish-bosheth “could not answer Abner a word again, because he feared him”. 2 Samuel 3:7–11
At David's demand he took his sister Michal from her husband Phaltiel and sent her back to David. 2 Samuel 3:14–16
When he heard that Abner was dead, “his hands were feeble, and all the Israelites were troubled”. 2 Samuel 4:1
Scripture gives Ish-bosheth no verdict. David, condemning his killers, called him “a righteous person” slain “in his own house upon his bed”. 2 Samuel 4:11
Mahanaim and the places of the reign
The united kingdom · tribe of Benjamin. Only places Scripture names are shown, each where the Atlas puts it.
Each mark sits at the year of the reign the Bible gives for it.
From the textScripture records nothing about worship in his reign.
David, king over Judah at Hebron
Each ribbon joins the two accounts of one matter, passage to passage.
Forty years old when he began to reign; reigned two years (2 Samuel 2:10). David reigned over Judah in Hebron seven years and six months (2 Samuel 2:11).
McFall gives Ish-bosheth's two years as 1010–1008 BC, with Abner the real ruler from 1008, and puts the deaths of both Abner and Ish-bosheth in 1003 BC.
Ussher dates his two quiet years from 1055 BC, then the long war; David became king over all Israel after his murder, in 1048 BC.
No BC years. Keil holds that Abner made him king only after recovering the land west of the Jordan, which may have taken five years.
Ussher read the two years as Ish-bosheth's reign before the long war with David's house began.[1]
Made king some years after Saul's death
Keil held that he reigned until his death and that Abner made him king only after retaking land lost to the Philistines, perhaps five years after Gilboa.[5]
The numbers are a later addition
Wellhausen held that the notes on his age and years break into the story, that he was still young, and that he must have reigned as long as David did in Hebron.[7]
Two years his, the rest Abner's
McFall dates his two years to 1010–1008 BC and treats Abner as the real ruler until both died in 1003 BC.[3]
Scripture does not name Ish-bosheth's mother. (The site's family data lists Ahinoam, Saul's wife, as his mother; no verse says so.)
Scripture records no anointing, no prophet and no verdict for him.
Scripture does not say where the rest of his body was buried; only his head is said to have been buried, in Abner's tomb.
1 Samuel 14:49 does not list him among Saul's sons.

Scholars' viewThis page takes Ish-bosheth of 2 Samuel to be the Esh-baal of Chronicles' lists of Saul's sons, as the site's person record does. Keil and Delitzsch (tr. 1866) hold that Esh-baal was his own name, and that “bosheth” (“shame”) later replaced “Baal” in it. 2 Samuel 2:8 1 Chronicles 8:33 1 Chronicles 9:39 [5]
